title: Empirical deployment signal playbook: triggers, probes, and procurement thresholds
creator: Priya Desai
description:
Goal: Produce a reproducible playbook that converts raw market signals about competitor model deployments and new open-model releases into operational triggers (probe experiments, procurement recommendations, and product contingency changes).

Scope: 1) Define a taxonomy of external signals (binary release events, gradual capacity announcements, pricing deltas, benchmark regressions, open-source forks). 2) Specify a minimal set of lightweight probes (latency/fallback tests, quality-canary prompts, cost-synthetic workload runs) that engineering can run in <24h. 3) Map signal severity to concrete responses: monitoring probes to run, procurement threshold rules for Dedicated/Private capacity, customer communication templates, and temporary routing policies in the Console. 4) Deliver an executable checklist, example dashboards and a short training doc for Solutions/GTM teams.

Deliverables: playbook doc (Confluence), 6 canonical probe scripts (bench harness + prompts), example alert rules for SLO dashboard, a small decision matrix (severity -> action), and a short runbook for on-call Platform/PM to follow when a high-severity signal fires.
acceptance_criteria: A Confluence playbook exists with the taxonomy, decision matrix, and step-by-step probe run instructions.
Probe scripts are checked into the model-monitoring repo with READMEs and can be executed by infra with <= 4 commands.

Three worked examples documented: (a) unexpected public release of a high-quality open model, (b) competitor hosted pricing cut in EU region, (c) vendor deprecation notice affecting a quantized runtime.
Alerting rules and dashboard templates are drafted and validated with Observability team (ENG), and sample alerts generate reproducible probes.
Procurement thresholds and templated communication artifacts are reviewed and approved by Finance and Legal stakeholders.
A 30-min training session for Solutions and GTM has been scheduled and materials are stored in the playbook.
